name: Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Symmetrical, diffuse thickening of the stratum corneum on palms and soles
Onset of keratoderma in infancy or early childhood
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with preserved epidermal architecture
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetrical diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with onset in early childhood plus either histopathological confirmation or positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical diffuse hyperkeratosis of palms and soles
searchTerms: symmetrical thick skin on palms and soles
evenly spread thickened skin on hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated thickened plaques on palmar and plantar surfaces
searchTerms: well-defined thick plaques on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fissuring and painful cracks in hyperkeratotic skin
searchTerms: fissuring with discomfort in callused areas
splitting and pain in hyperkeratotic skin

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to affected areas
searchTerms: localized mild itching on affected skin
excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Secondary bacterial or fungal infections in fissures
searchTerms: bacterial or fungal infections in fissures
nail changes linked to thickened skin

occasional.symptomName: Pain exacerbated by mechanical stress on palms and soles
searchTerms: pain worsened by use or pressure on hands and feet
mechanical stress causing palm and sole pain
pain triggered by hand and foot activity

occasional.symptomName: Hyperkeratotic lesions extending to dorsal aspects of hands and feet
searchTerms: thickened skin spreading to back of hands and feet
lesions reaching dorsal hand and foot areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild scaling and peeling at lesion margins
searchTerms: mild skin scaling and peeling at edges

rare.symptomName: Associated pseudoainhum (constriction bands leading to autoamputation)
searchTerms: constriction bands causing finger or toe autoamputation

rare.notes: Very rare but reported in some syndromic forms
searchTerms: development of skin cancers in thickened palm and sole areas

rare.symptomName: Associated hearing loss in syndromic variants

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing compact hyperkeratosis with preserved epidermal layers
Negative fungal cultures unless secondary infection present
imaging: Rarely required; X-rays may show soft tissue changes if pseudoainhum present
genetic: Mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT1, KRT9) in some familial cases
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic diffuse palmoplantar thickening

distinguishingFeatures: Discrete punctate keratotic lesions rather than diffuse plaques
Later onset compared to diffuse PPK
Linear or striate hyperkeratosis along fingers and palms
Associated with systemic diseases or exposures

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Development of constriction bands (pseudoainhum) risking autoamputation
Signs of secondary infection or systemic involvement
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Fischer J, et al. Palmoplantar keratodermas: clinical and molecular classification. J Dtsch Dermatol Ges. 2016.
